meta.author: Śrīla Bhakti Vinod Ṭhākur
meta.first_line: bhāi re! śarīra avidyā-jāla jaḍendriya tāhe kāla

text: tāra madhye jihvā ati    lobhamaya sudurmati
translation: O brother! The body is a net of illusion, and the material senses are one’s enemies; they throw the soul into the ocean of mundanity. Among the senses, the tongue is the most voracious and wicked. It is very difficult to conquer the tongue in this world.

text: kṛṣṇa baḍa dayāmaya    karibāre jihvā jaya
translation: Kṛṣṇa is very merciful: to conquer the tongue He has given us His remnants. Accept this nectarean food, sing the glories of Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa, and with love call out, “Chaitanya! Nitāi!”
N.B. On Harivāsar-tithis (days on which devotees fast from grains) the above song beginning *Bhāi re! Śarīra avidyā-jāla* is not customarily sung because it mentions grain prasādam (anna).
